analysis.title: The Global Volatility Pulse: Mid-term risk: Not too late to hedge
key_insights: Barclays does not think the recent sell-off marks the end of the AI trade, but says uncertainty over the sustainability and financing of the AI capex cycle is real. The build-out increasingly needs debt financing, and history shows rising leverage and capex tends to coincide with higher equity volatility.

The midterms could be another risk-off catalyst. Democratic control is generally viewed as less favorable for parts of the AI complex (hyperscalers, semis, utilities, data-center development). Barclays expects the impact to be more about sentiment and pricing of future regulatory risk than immediate legislative change.
The S&P implied move around the midterm election has risen to roughly 1%. That is not outsized versus other near-term catalysts: Friday's NFP is priced at 99bps.

Normalized by VIX, election risk pricing has stayed stable. Most of the rise in the absolute implied move reflects the broader repricing of equity volatility during the sell-off, not a specific election premium.

The probability of a Democratic sweep or of Democrats winning the Texas governor race, which may be the most important race for AI infrastructure, has been rising for some time without disrupting markets. The VIX-adjusted election implied move has barely changed.
Election-linked S&P option open interest (4-Nov expiry) is in line with nearby expiries, so there is little sign of unusual election hedging.

Midterms have typically been followed by a risk-on move, but the S&P is already up roughly 10% this year versus historical midterm-year performance of around flat. That may leave less room for the usual post-election upside.
With downside skew historically steep, Barclays recommends SPY put spreads and down-and-out puts as hedges.

Gold failed to catch a bid during the recent equity sell-off. Its average daily underperformance versus Treasuries and the yen on days of S&P weakness over the past month ranks among the largest in history, partly due to strong Treasury performance and recent bearishness on gold.
Lula's surprise reelection sparked a sharp Brazil sell-off and record daily outflows from EWZ, which Barclays reads as investors not buying the dip.

The Barclays Equity Euphoria Indicator 1-month moving average is 10.6%, 1.31 standard deviations above its long-term average of 7.2%. It is above the lows seen around the March and July Nasdaq corrections, so speculative retail investors remain engaged.

About 190 STOXX 600 companies, roughly 25% of index market cap, report over the next two weeks. Misses have been punished more than beats rewarded, so the reaction function is asymmetric. Burberry, National Grid and United Utilities screen as relatively cheap earnings vol, while Vonovia, Ahold Delhaize and Richemont screen rich.
SX5E's roughly 6% retreat from its 11 Aug high has been orderly, with realised vol near the lows of past selloffs of similar size and pace. 1-month correlation is 19%, an unremarkable rise.

SMI outperformed SX5E by about 10pp over the past month on its defensive tilt to Health Care and Staples, a historically extreme gap. SXXP's roughly 2% monthly gain masks a defensive rotation, with Health Care and Food & Beverage outperforming near 25-year extremes.
SMI's implied vol versus SX5E and call skew both sit near median, so Barclays says upside optionality to express further defensive strength looks reasonably priced.

sector_views.rationale: Defensive rotation has driven SMI to historically extreme outperformance of about 10pp vs SX5E over the past month. Health Care and Food & Beverage outperformance is near 25-year extremes.

earnings_insights: Around 190 STOXX 600 companies (about 25% of index market cap) are scheduled to report over the next two weeks. Earnings delivery has been strong so far, but median price action has been negatively skewed, with misses punished more than beats rewarded.

EU earnings vol screen (implied earnings move vs average realised move over the past two years, plus VolScore): Burberry, National Grid and United Utilities screen as relatively cheap, Vonovia, Ahold Delhaize and Richemont as richer. Screen only, not a recommendation.
NVDA earnings is marked on the forward-vol term-structure chart (Figure 1) as an upcoming event in the 4-20 Nov window. AMD reports after the close on 3-Nov per the chart footnote.

tension_points.bull_case: Midterms have historically been followed by a risk-on move, and the recent sell-off does not mark the end of the AI trade. Options pricing shows no outsized election premium.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty around AI capex sustainability and financing is real, and a Democratic win is seen as less AI-friendly. The S&P is already up about 10% YTD versus a flat historical midterm-year path, so there may be less post-election upside. Options markets look complacent, with unusual hedging absent.

theme_stances.evidence: Yet options markets hardly appear alarmed.
